newsitem.title: USA: Stiglitz sees no imbalances in U.S. economy - RFTV.
newsitem.headline: Stiglitz sees no imbalances in U.S. economy - RFTV.

text.p: White House Economic Adviser Joseph Stiglitz Friday said the U.S. economy was in a healthy state with no imbalances showing at this time.
Interviewed on Reuters Financial Television, he said that there was enormous strength in the household sector going into next year and that exports should be buoyed by rebounding economies overseas.
"We're in a very good situation for the economy right now," he said.

He said the Council of Economic Advisers had a meeting with some of the country's leading economic forecasters and "the unanimous consensus among this group was that there was essentially no imbalances in our economy -- a remarkable state of affairs for an economy at this stage of the recovery."
He said that while consumer spending had been weak in the past quarter, as he looked at where the economy was heading, "we see enormous strength in this sector - in the household sector."
Turning to exports, he said that as he looks overseas he sees a number of ecomomies rebounding and that this should benefit U.S. exports.
"Given the low inflation, given the strength of our increases in productivity, the American firms can really do very well in the international markets," he said.
Stiglitz also said that the low levels of unemployment in the United States -- it was 5.2 percent in October -- are sustainable without igniting additional inflation.

Asked about the White House forecast for 1997 showing economic growth of 2.3 percent, Stiglitz said that the economy may be stronger that his estimate but that the administation preferred to error on the side of caution in these matters.
"We deliberately choose conservative numbers," he said, adding that "we think the economy may very well be stronger."
